title: Add Usage Insights CSV export + BI ingestion example
author: Alex Martinez
description:
Context: Customers (and internal finance partners) want route+model cost breakdowns they can pull into BI. The console supports CSV export; this PR adds a runnable example that hits the Usage Insights export endpoints, downloads the generated CSV via signed URL, and loads it into a warehouse-friendly format.

What’s in this PR: (1) New Python example: scripts/usage_insights/export_and_load.py Creates an export job for a given time range + filters, polls job status with backoff, downloads the CSV, and (optionally) loads into BigQuery or writes parquet. (2) Sample config + env var docs (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BASE_URL, WORKSPACE_ID, PROJECT_ID). (3) README updates: step-by-step instructions, common failure modes (permissions, large ranges causing timeouts), and notes on reconciling totals vs billing.

Notes/assumptions: - Export endpoint follows the async lifecycle: POST /v1/usage/insights/exports -> GET /v1/usage/insights/exports/{id} -> GET signed download_url. - Script is intentionally conservative with time ranges (defaults to 7d) to avoid the known long-range query behavior tracked in SUP-24863. - This example does not attempt scheduled exports (out of scope for initial release); it’s designed to be run ad-hoc or wired into a customer’s existing cron.

Checklist: - [x] Example runs against staging (hosted) and local mock server - [x] README includes RBAC caveat (must have cost:read + export:write) - [x] No secrets in repo; keys only via env vars - [x] Added basic unit test for CSV parsing and schema normalization

Screenshots: N/A (CLI example).

conversation: Dylan Brooks (review): This is great for beta enablement. Two asks: (1) please align endpoint paths with the v1 contract naming (I think it’s /v1/usage-insights/exports in the latest draft), and (2) add a note about data freshness banners (customers will ask why “today” looks low).

Alex Martinez (author): Good catch. Updated paths to match /v1/usage/insights/exports per the merged API PR, and added a “freshness” section that prints the job’s data_through timestamp when present + README note on partial-day windows.
Chloe Martin (review): Can we avoid hammering the status endpoint? Current polling is every 2s for 5 minutes. Please implement exponential backoff and cap at ~30s. Also, handle 429 with Retry-After.
Alex Martinez (author): Done. Polling now uses backoff (2s -> 4 -> 8 -> 16 -> 30s max) and honors Retry-After on 429/503. Added a short note about rate limits and a --poll-max-seconds flag.

Elliot Price (review): README looks solid. Minor wording: prefer “endpoint” over “route” in customer-facing docs, but keep “route” when referencing the dimension name in CSV columns. Also add link to console docs page (placeholder is fine).

Alex Martinez (author): Updated terminology per guidance and added a “Column glossary” section (route_template, model_family, model_version, tokens_in/out, cache_hit_tokens, retry_count). Linked to the console help center draft page placeholder URL.
Markus Klein (review): For BI load, BigQuery is great, but can we also show a generic “load to Snowflake” approach? Even a pseudo-step would help.

Alex Martinez (author): Added a short “Other warehouses” section with CSV->stage->COPY patterns and a note that signed URLs are time-limited. Kept it non-vendor-specific to avoid maintaining multiple SDK examples.
Dylan Brooks (approval): Approved. Thanks for adding the freshness and backoff details; those were the main footguns I’ve seen in early beta.
CI (bot): All checks passed: unit-tests, lint, formatting, security-scan.
release_notes: Examples repo: added a runnable script to export Usage Insights CSV via async export endpoints and load results into BI workflows (BigQuery/parquet), plus README guidance on permissions, freshness, and troubleshooting.
